Implement michi's 0.12 API cleanup: one way to build each response (AgentResponse), removing duplicate standalone renderers. Repo orin-dx/michi. Branch from `origin/fix/pipeline-start-record` (it contains the 0.11 fixes and changesets that are about to release) as `refactor/one-render-path`. Read AGENTS.md and PRINCIPLES.md first (rules: prefix shell commands with `rtk`; `cargo nextest run`; no unwrap/expect in lib; every pub item documented; NAPI `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export; comments plain and wrapped at 120 cols; a claim needs a test that fails when broken — check with a mutant and revert). Commit (conventional, `refactor(core)!: ...`; no session links or Claude-Session trailers) and push the branch (normal push, never force, never main). Do NOT open a PR.

Policy context: pre-1.0, breaking changes are fine and we remove legacy surface instead of shimming. The only consumer of michi is monokl (Rust); it uses none of the items below. Nothing uses the npm package's standalone renderers.

## Remove (NAPI / `@orin-dx/michi`, in crates/michi-core/src/napi/)
- `renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline` (napi/outcome.rs), `renderStatus` (napi/toon.rs), `renderAlreadyDone` and `alreadyDone` (+ the `AlreadyDone` JS object type if it then has no use), and `renderDomainError`. Each duplicates `AgentResponse.partialSuccess/pipeline/status/alreadyDone/error` + `renderText()`.
- Replace `renderDomainError`'s one unique capability, the GitHub Actions annotation (its `githubAnnotation` flag), with a new export `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message) => string` that calls Rust `DomainError::render_github_annotation()` (crates/michi-core/src/error.rs ~:459). Validate `code` the same way renderDomainError did; same input limits/budget style as sibling exports.
- KEEP `renderToon`, `renderKv` (the list alone), `renderHints`, `appendHints`, `renderRecovery`, `truncate`, `parseRetryAfter`, `nextRetryDelay`, `isRetryableStatus`, the `AgentResponse` class.
- Remove now-dead NAPI helpers/cost code only used by removed exports; keep the byte-budget accounting correct for what remains (napi/cost.rs, napi/input.rs).

## Remove (Rust, michi-core)
- `resilience::render_already_done` (~resilience.rs:465) — use `AgentResponse::already_done(operation, summary)` + `.hint`.
- `resilience::already_done(Option<String>) -> AlreadyDone` and the `AlreadyDone` enum (~:439-455), unless something else in the workspace still needs them (check michi-pipeline too); remove their root re-exports in lib.rs.
- `StatusResponse`'s own hints channel: the `hints` field and `hints()` builder (status.rs ~:56-68). Status hints come from `AgentResponse::hint`. Keep `StatusResponse::render` if it is still the type's own render used elsewhere (RunRecord-style); otherwise judge by PRINCIPLES.md and explain.
- Keep the types' own `render()` methods (DomainError, PartialSuccess, Pipeline, StatusResponse) — they are what AgentResponse composes and what Rust callers use directly; this task is about the duplicate free functions and second hint channel.

## Update everything that references them
- Tests: Rust tests, snapshot tests (`cargo insta` — review, don't blindly accept), ui-fail tests, fuzz targets (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/*`), Node tests in packages/michi-node/__test__/ (rewrite coverage of behaviour that still exists through `AgentResponse` methods, e.g. duplicate-index throw via `AgentResponse.partialSuccess`; delete tests only for behaviour that is truly gone), scripts/smoke/*, examples, benches.
- Docs: packages/michi-node/README.md API tables, README.md, docs/spec/03-rust-api.md, docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md, docs/spec/05-scope-and-quality.md (instability table mentions `AlreadyDone`, `already_done()`), docs/spec/01 file tree comments, AGENTS.md module table if affected, rustdoc. Add a short entry to docs/spec/06-decisions.md: "One render path per outcome" — what was removed, why (duplicates of AgentResponse; legacy surface we would otherwise promise at 1.0), and that `renderGithubAnnotation` keeps the one unique capability.
- Changesets: follow the project's changeset standard strictly (user-first, per audience). Write TWO new files: `.changeset/js-one-render-path.md` with front matter `michi-node: minor` (JS terms only) and `.changeset/core-one-render-path.md` with `michi-core: minor` (Rust terms only). Each: lead line starting `**Breaking:**` saying what changed for the reader, then short bullets: what was removed → what to use instead (one line each, with a before → after example where useful), and the new `renderGithubAnnotation` in the JS one. No implementation detail. Look at the existing `.changeset/js-*.md` and `core-*.md` for the voice. Do not edit the existing 0.11 changesets.

## Verify (judge by exit codes)
- `just check` and `just test` (Rust + Node). Scaling tests are wall-clock ratios and can flake under machine load; if only `michi-core::scaling` fails, rerun it alone and report load (`uptime`).
- A mutant for `renderGithubAnnotation` (e.g. return the plain text render) must fail a Node test.
- `rg` for every removed name across the repo (excluding CHANGELOG.md files and docs/superpowers/) returns nothing.

## Report
Branch + commit SHA, files changed (stat), removed items and their replacements, the two changeset texts verbatim, test count before/after and which tests were removed vs rewritten, mutant result, check exit codes, and anything you chose to keep with the reason. Under ~800 words.

Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- Rendering makes output syntactically safe, not trustworthy: it keeps one value from creating extra lines, fields or cells, and it does not judge what a value says. See the [trust model](docs/spec/02-toon-format.md#trust-model).
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Small default dependency set

The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.

- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.

### 4. Doesn't duplicate an existing primitive

Check `hints` / `recovery` / `idempotency` / `status` / `error` / `mcp` first. Verify the distinction concretely — don't assume novelty from a vibe.

- "This looks similar to X" means go read X's source, not assume it's covered.
- Example: a proposed "diagnostics" primitive looked adjacent to `idempotency::PartialSuccess` — until actually reading `PartialSuccess`'s doc comment showed it's scoped to multi-step _mutating_ operations, not read-path degradation. They turned out genuinely distinct, but that took checking, not assuming either way.

### 5. Deviations get tracked, not silently absorbed

Where the final shape diverges from the original ask or an earlier draft, it goes in a Design Decisions table. Spec and code should never quietly drift apart.

---

## Split the decision from the signal

Gate 1's ceiling ("stay generic" vs. "real tools need real sophistication") isn't a tension to compromise on — it's usually an architecture problem. Separate the _domain-specific decision_ from the _universal signal_.

**Worked example: truncation.** Deciding _which_ items survive a budget is tool-specific — personalized-PageRank over a call graph, a statistical outlier-preserving sampler, a simple first-N cutoff. None of that belongs in michi. But _reporting_ what got cut, in a consistent agent-readable shape, is exactly what every tool needs regardless of how it decided.

That split shipped as `michi_core::truncation` (API in [`docs/spec/03-rust-api.md`](docs/spec/03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)): `TruncationOutcome<T>` holds what was kept and the total before the cut, `hint(guidance)` gives the standard `help[]` line, `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` are the two strategies michi ships, and `AgentResponse::truncation` sets the count and the hint together. Where the shipped shape differs from the first sketch (a derived `truncated()` instead of a stored flag, a public `new()`, `truncate_by_size` instead of `truncate_by_bytes`), the reasons are in [`docs/spec/06-decisions.md`](docs/spec/06-decisions.md).

A caller with a genuinely novel heuristic never has to fit their algorithm into michi's shape — they wrap whatever they decided with `TruncationOutcome::new` and get the same hint/report format everyone else gets. Michi owns the contract, not the heuristic.

**When a new primitive seems too domain-specific to generalize, ask whether it splits this way first.** Often only half of it actually is.

---

## How work gets done

Heuristics, not hard rules — process needs contextual judgment the content checklist doesn't.

### 1. TDD, always

Failing test first, verified red for the right reason, then implementation, then green. No implementation code without a preceding red test.

### 2. Independent verification before "done"

A separate pass re-checks against the spec by running the actual output — not by trusting the implementer's self-report or re-reading the diff.

- Per-task review alone has missed real bugs that a separately-scoped validation pass, checking actual wire output, caught.
- "Every task's reviewer said pass" and "the feature actually works" are different questions. Both need answering.

### 3. Verify before asserting

Claims about external state — a registry's current contents, another project's actual spec, a dependency's real behavior — get checked directly, not recalled from memory or assumed from a plausible-sounding claim.

- Can't quickly re-verify something? Say so rather than asserting confidence.

### 4. History is append-only

Superseded plans/specs get a notice pointing at what replaced them, not a rewrite pretending they always said the current thing.

- A plan document that was correct when written stays as written. Corrections happen in new commits, not retroactive edits to old ones.

### 5. Publish/release gates are earned

Passing a component's own tests isn't "ready to ship."

- Release checks should cover package contents, compatibility promises, security, and the intended release scope. Consumer integration can be a post-release check when a published package is needed to perform that integration.

### 6. Invariant enforcement policy

Three patterns apply at different layers. Pick the right one for the layer — don't invent a fourth.

- **Infallible constructors normalize.** `new()` clamps inputs to valid ranges silently (e.g. `jitter_factor` to `[0.0, 1.0]`, `base_delay` to `≤ max_delay`). Never `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code. Expose a `try_new()` or `validate()` alongside for callers who want explicit error signals — but these are additive, they don't replace the normalizing constructor.
- **Rendering never fails silently, and never reports a failure as success.** Two cases:
  - Input that can always be made safe is sanitized at the render layer, and that `render*()` returns `String`: escape or replace structural characters so one value cannot create extra lines, fields or cells.
  - Input whose shape can be wrong (TOON row length against its fields, a structural character in a header name) is validated, and the free functions return `Result` (`render_toon`, `ToonDocument::validate`, `toon::list`). There is no `debug_assert!` fallback: debug and release builds behave the same.
  - A builder that must always produce a response (`AgentResponse`) renders a validation failure as an error block and marks the response as an error on every surface: the text body, the JSON `isError`, and MCP `isError`. Callers can check `AgentResponse::is_error()` before sending.
- **Wire it in or document it as opt-in.** A `validate()` or `try_new()` that has no caller is documentation masquerading as validation. Any new validation method must either be called from at least one mandatory code path (not just tests) or carry an explicit `/// Caller opt-in — not called automatically` doc comment.
- **Empty strings are accepted everywhere.** michi doesn't validate business rules — constructors accept empty strings unconditionally. The render result for an empty field is an empty field, not an error. This is a deliberate contract, not an oversight; document it if adding a new constructor where it might surprise a reader.

---

## Using this document

- **Content questions** ("should X be a michi primitive?") → the five gates above, in order. Stop at the first "no."
- **Process questions** ("is this ready to ship / merge / call done?") → the five heuristics, weighed together, not mechanically checked off.
- **When they pull in different directions** — a genuinely useful pattern seen only once, a process shortcut that would ship something faster — that's not a bug in the framework. It's the signal to slow down and think it through explicitly, rather than pick the convenient answer.

- **Content questions** ("should X be a michi primitive?") → the five gates above, in order. Stop at the first "no."
- **Process questions** ("is this ready to ship / merge / call done?") → the five heuristics, weighed together, not mechanically checked off.
- **When they pull in different directions** — a genuinely useful pattern seen only once, a process shortcut that would ship something faster — that's not a bug in the framework. It's the signal to slow down and think it through explicitly, rather than pick the convenient answer.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail when a diff changes public Rust API without touching any documentation.

Usage: python3 scripts/check-api-docs.py [BASE [HEAD]] [--pr-body TEXT]

BASE..HEAD defaults to origin/main..HEAD (diffed from their merge base, like a PR). The PR body comes from --pr-body
or the PR_BODY environment variable; a line starting `No spec change needed: <reason>` skips the check.

Public API means added or removed `pub` item lines (fn, struct, enum, trait, type, const, static, mod, use, union,
and `pub name: Type` fields) in crates/*/src/**/*.rs, outside test files and `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Lines that are
identical on both sides (code moved between files) cancel out. Enum variants, trait items and anything a macro
generates are not visible to this check.
"""

import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SRC = re.compile(r"^crates/[^/]+/src/.+\.rs$")
TEST_FILE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(tests?|benches|examples)/|(^|/)tests?\.rs$|_tests?\.rs$")
DOCS = re.compile(r"^(docs/spec/|docs/adr/|crates/[^/]+/README\.md$|README\.md$|ARCHITECTURE\.md$)")
KINDS = "fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|use|union"

import os, sys, time, zlib

root = "/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.git/objects"
out = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
now = time.time()
for d in os.listdir(root):
    if len(d) != 2:
        continue
    for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(root, d)):
        p = os.path.join(root, d, f)
        if now - os.path.getmtime(p) > 40 * 60:
            continue
        data = zlib.decompress(open(p, "rb").read())
        header, _, body = data.partition(b"\0")
        if not header.startswith(b"blob"):
            continue
        first = body[:200].split(b"\n")[0].decode("utf-8", "replace")
        open(os.path.join(out, d + f), "wb").write(body)
        print(d + f, len(body), first[:100])

## Data Composition & Render Flow

`michi` provides two main entry points for formatting output:

1. **`response::AgentResponse` (Fluent Builder)**: Composes TOON lists, KV items, `help[]` hints, and recovery guidance into a unified output buffer. Supports assistant/user audience routing and direct conversion to MCP `CallToolResult`.
2. **Standalone DTOs**: `DomainError`, `StatusResponse` and `AlreadyDone` render themselves directly into agent-readable KV blocks or GitHub Actions annotations without passing through `AgentResponse`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph primitives["Primitives"]
        toon["michi-core::toon"]
        kv["michi-core::kv"]
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `truncation` | `TruncationOutcome`: what a cap on a list cut, however the caller chose the survivors |
| `error` | `DomainError` (with `ErrorCode`/`ErrorClass`): the one agent-facing error, with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `redact` | Best-effort redaction: known secrets, URL userinfo and common credential shapes (`redact_common_shapes`); applied by `DomainError::from_error` |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
# michi — MVP Implementation Plan

> **Historical record.** This dated document shows what was planned or decided at the time; much of it has since changed. Don't implement from it. For current behavior, see [`docs/spec/`](../spec/README.md), [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [ADRs](../adr/README.md).

> orin-dx · Draft · June 2026
- The shipped design splits it: `DomainError` is the pure data/render type — what [03-rust-api.md](03-rust-api.md) documents.
- `Error` is a `thiserror`-derived enum with a `Domain(DomainError)` variant alongside always-compiled `InvalidInput`/`NotFound` variants; the original intent was room for execution-layer variants (`Http`, `Timeout`, `StepFailed`) once the `pipeline` crate (Plan 2) landed.
- **That's not how it shipped.** `crates/michi-pipeline` defines its own `ExecutionError` enum (`Http`, `Timeout`, `Failed`, `CircuitOpen`, `StepFailed`, `Cancelled`, `Interrupted`, `AmbiguousOutcome`, `Panicked`, and since 0.6 `DeadlinePassed`; plan validation has its own `PlanError` since the 2026-10-21 redesign) rather than adding variants to `michi_core::Error`. `impl From<ExecutionError> for DomainError` converts at the boundary instead. `michi_core::Error` itself still has only `InvalidInput`/`NotFound`/`Domain` — verified against current source, not extended. This keeps `michi-pipeline`'s error surface independently versioned alongside the crate it belongs to, consistent with the "independent release cadence" rationale above, rather than coupling it back into `michi-core`.

### `idempotency::already_done()` only checks — it doesn't render

- An early draft had one function do both.
- michi owns no persistence layer, so it has no way to know on its own whether an operation already happened — only your store does.
- Splitting check from render is the honest shape: `already_done()` takes what your lookup found and classifies it; `render_already_done()` renders regardless of how you detected the no-op.

### `IdempotencyKey::new()` takes one pre-combined string, not `(operation, stable_input)`

- A caller that wants an operation-name-plus-input key builds it themselves (`format!("{operation}:{stable_input}")`) before calling `new`, or uses `from_hash` for the hashed variant.
- `from_hash` uses FNV-1a, not SHA-256 — idempotency keys need stability and low collision, not cryptographic security.
- This crate has no `sha2` dependency at all today — it was removed along with the rest of the unused `cache` feature (see the crate-boundary entry below).

content.content:
- `RetryConfig::try_new` rejects a zero `max_delay` because zero drops a server's `Retry-After`. Setting `cfg.max_delay = Duration::ZERO` afterwards made `next_retry_delay(&cfg, 0, 0.5, Some(60 s))` return 0 ns, a hot retry against a server that asked for a minute. `michi-pipeline` re-exports `RetryConfig`.
- `DomainError`'s builder keeps `MAY_HAVE_TAKEN_EFFECT_HINT` present exactly while a `Timeout` is not retryable. `e.retryable = true` on a timeout kept the hint, so the JSON said `retryable: true` and the help said not to retry blindly; `e.code = Timeout` on a `RateLimited` error gave a retryable timeout with no hint, the unsafe retry the hint exists for. `michi-pipeline`'s own `AmbiguousOutcome` conversion wrote `retryable = false` directly and so skipped the hint; with the builder a timeout source now carries core's verify-first hint, and the pipeline adds its own `VERIFY_BEFORE_RETRY_HINT` only when core's is absent, so the agent reads one, not two.
- `PartialSuccess` took the same operation index in `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` (op 0 rendered completed and failed, `exit=1`), and a completed operation's `reason` was accepted and silently not rendered.

At 1.0 a public field freezes the layout and makes such a rule unenforceable for good. `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph` already keep their fields private behind getters, so core now follows them where it matters.

- **Private, with getters:** `DomainError` (`code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()`, `is_retryable()`), `RetryConfig` (`max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()`, `jitter_factor()`) and `PartialSuccess` (`completed()`, `failed()`, `skipped()`, built with `try_new`, which returns `DuplicateOpIndex`). `Section` went private the same day ("Envelope facts have one source"). The compiler is the proof: `compile_fail,E0616` doctests on each type assert the error code for the audit's field writes.
- **Still public:** plain records with no rule across fields: `KvItem`, `ProvenanceEntry`, `FailedOp`, `RecoveryHint`, `StatusItem`, `StatusResponse`, `PipelineStep`, `Pipeline`, `ContentBlock`, `CallToolResult`, and the newtypes.
- **States the domain forbids:** `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason, so none can be dropped) and `SkippedOp`; the JS `renderPartialSuccess` takes the same two shapes, rejects a non-null `reason` on a completed op and throws on a repeated index. `Pipeline.id` is removed: nothing rendered it, `renderPipeline` passed an empty string, and `RunRecord::to_pipeline` filled it for no reader. Rejected: rendering it (`pipeline: <id>`), which would change a document no consumer asked to change; `RunRecord::run_id()` already gives the id.
- **`CallToolResult.structured_content` is `Option<JsonObject>`.** It was a `String` where empty meant none, checked only by `try_new` or at serialization, both behind `serde`, so a default-feature caller could build a result that could not serialize. `JsonObject::new` checks the text in every build with a strict RFC 8259 checker in `mcp.rs` that applies `serde_json`'s limits (127 levels, no lone surrogate escapes, finite numbers); a property test compares the two. michi's own renderers wrap their writers' output directly. The field stays public: the type now carries the rule. The wire shape is unchanged.
- **`michi_core::Error` and `Result` are removed.** No michi API returned them (every fallible function has its own error type; `michi-pipeline` converts to `DomainError`), monokl builds `DomainError` directly, and `Error::InvalidInput`/`NotFound` duplicated `ErrorCode` minus hints, recovery and causes. ADR 9 says such surface goes before 1.0. `class()` and `is_retryable()` live on `DomainError`; `is_retryable()` is `true` exactly when `class()` is `Transient`.
- **One convention for builders and getters** (spec 03, "API conventions"): builders are bare and consuming (`x(v)` sets or appends one, `xs(vec)` replaces a list); getters are bare, `is_x()` for a `bool`, and `get_x()` only when a builder of the same type holds the bare name, as `std::process::Command::get_args` does. Considered: `with_x` builders (would rename every builder in core and `michi-pipeline` to free a few getter names) and getters named after their type (`recovery_hint()` would read as `AgentResponse`'s appending builder of the same name). Applied: `StatusResponse::with_hints` became `hints`; `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]` like every other renderer; `DomainError::render()` and `render_json()` became `render(OutputFormat)`, like `AgentResponse`; text-only types keep `render()`. `DomainError::context(prefix)` replaces the field write `e.message = format!(…)` the docs used to suggest, and `retry_after(None)` clears a delay.
- **Derives that were missing:** `Hash` on `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass`, `Display` on `ErrorCode` (its label), `PartialEq` on `DomainError`, `Eq` on `AttemptRecord`, and `FromStr` plus `Borrow<str>` on `StepId` and `RunId`, so `"x".parse::<StepId>()` works and a `BTreeMap<StepId, _>` is looked up with a `&str`. `Hint`'s `Eq`/`Hash` belong to the hints module's owner and are not part of this change.

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — Outcomes compose into one response

The architecture audit of 0.10.0 (finding 4) found that errors, partial success, status and pipeline state did not compose with `AgentResponse`. Five roots rendered five documents, and only `AgentResponse` and `DomainError` produced JSON or a `CallToolResult`, in two shapes: `recovery` was an array in one and an object or `null` in the other, and `error.rs` told callers not to wrap a `DomainError` in a response. `PartialSuccess::render` wrote a root `recovery` table, a key `AgentResponse` writes too, so the batch spec 07 section 4 was widened for (results, per-op outcomes, budget, provenance) could not be one valid document. JS could not get an error's JSON at all. ADR 9 calls michi a response contract for errors, status and partial success; only lists got the full contract.

- **One composer, one writer.** Every outcome is a part of `AgentResponse`. `error(e)` holds one `DomainError`; `partial_success(name, ps)`, `status(s)`, `pipeline(name, p)` and `already_done(operation, summary)` add ordinary `Section`s (`Toon` or `Kv`), so validation, the root-key check, the cell cap, `totalCount`, the budget roll-up and the JSON `sections` all apply unchanged. Their hints join the one `help` block and their recovery hints the one `recovery` table. Each type's own render (`DomainError::render`/`to_call_tool_result`, `PartialSuccess::render`, `StatusResponse::render`, `Pipeline::render` and so `RunRecord::render`, `render_already_done`) is that response's render, so a lone outcome and a composed one cannot drift; the standalone forms turn the cell cap off, as they never cut a cell. No new `SectionBody` variant and no trait: rejected as parallel concepts next to the section model that already renders every surface. Rejected too: `to_section()` on each type, which would leave the failed ops' recovery and the status hints for the caller to move by hand.
- **One error shape.** In JSON the error is `"error": {"code", "message", "causes", "retryable"}` beside the response's `hints` and `recovery` arrays. `DomainError::render(OutputFormat::Json)`, its serde form and its `schemars` schema are that envelope (`body`, `error`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError`), so an MCP client parses one shape whether or not the error came with data. Rejected: keeping hints and recovery inside the `error` object, which would give the one `help` block two sources. `retry_after` stays off the wire ("Two facts per failure" and the serde decision stand).
- **The error block leads**, as `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code`, the reserved error keys, so no caller name can take them. One per response (a second `error()` replaces the first). A validation failure never hides it: the failure joins its causes (superseded wording, see "Response consistency" below; this said a response with both rendered the `toon_validation_failed` error for the key `error`, which hid the caller's error from the text while the JSON still carried it). `is_error()`, the JSON `isError` and MCP `isError` are true.
- **Partial success is one table**, `name[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, a row per op sorted by index (unique since `try_new`), `status` `completed`/`failed`/`skipped`, `reason` the failure reason, skip token or `null`. The quoted summary line is gone: the `status` column says the same, and as a fixed root key it collided when two batches composed. Rejected: the three tables (`completed`, `failed`, `skipped` are fixed root names a caller's sections or a second batch collide with) and a nested object per batch (a new section kind and JSON kind, and nested tables are outside the subset the strict decoder checks). A partial batch does not set `isError`: the call answered; the caller adds `error()` or `as_error()` when it failed as a whole.
- **Status** is a `Kv` section `status` (`tool`, `description`) and the `items` table, with each `KvValue` turned into the cell that renders the same token (a float rounded to its decimals, a duration as `1.5s`). **Pipeline** is a `Toon` section; `michi-pipeline` composes a run with `pipeline(name, record.to_pipeline())` and `error(record.error()?.into())`, and needs no API change. **Already done** is a `Kv` section `already_done`.
- **NAPI** gets the same parts on the `AgentResponse` class: `error(code, message, causes?, retryable?)`, `partialSuccess(name, …)`, `pipeline(name, steps)`, `status(toolName, description, items)` and `alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, each with the standalone function's input limits and charged to the response's 16 MiB total (an error replaces its slot). `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` then cover errors, which no export did before. The standalone `render*` functions stay as text conveniences over the same writer.
- **Rendered output that moves:** `DomainError` JSON (and serde and schema) is the envelope above; `PartialSuccess` text is the one table, and an empty report is `partial_success: []` and `totalCount: 0`; an empty `Pipeline` (so `RunRecord::render` of a run with no steps) is `step: []` and `totalCount: 0`; a `StatusResponse` with no items is `items: []` and `totalCount: 0`. `DomainError` text, status and pipeline tables with rows, and the already-done text are byte-identical. `AgentResponse::render_hints_only` now includes an error's hints, as the `help` block does.
- **Proof:** `tests/compose_outcomes.rs` renders the spec 07 batch as one document checked by the strict decoder and as one JSON object, has a probe per type that could not compose before, and a property test mixes every outcome type with hostile text and checks one valid document, one JSON object and one `help`, `recovery` and `error` key. `michi-pipeline/tests/compose.rs` composes a failed run with its error.
- **Not changed:** a validation failure (`toon_validation_failed`) still has `isError` and its `error:` lines but no JSON `error` object; its code is not an `ErrorCode`, and giving it one would widen the schema's code enum for a michi-internal failure. (Superseded by "Response consistency" below: the failure is now an `error` object with a string code, and no `ErrorCode` is added.)

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — Response consistency

An independent review of the composed stack found a response that said two things: the text and the JSON disagreed, or one source of hints dropped another's. Each was reproduced as a failing test first (`tests/response_consistency.rs`). It amends "Outcomes compose into one response" (the error block and the "Not changed" bullet), the JSON `totalCount` bullet of "Envelope implementation deviations" and the JSON sentence of "One definitive empty state".

- **The caller's error is never hidden.** A `DomainError` and a validation failure (an invalid section, or two blocks writing one root key) used to collide on the key `error`, so the text read `error: toon_validation_failed` with "duplicate root key 'error'", a key the caller never used, while the JSON still said `external_failure`. Now the caller's error leads on every surface and stays the JSON `error` (code, message, `retryable`); the failure is added as its last cause, `<code>: <message>`, the form the NAPI exports throw, and a failed section writes no lines of its own. A collision still drops the sections, so the body is the error block alone. `isError` stays true. Considered: putting the failure first and the caller's error in its causes (the agent would read michi's bug before the tool's real failure, and `retryable` would be lost), and a separate root key for the failure (a twelfth reserved key and a second error shape). The failure is a cause because it is one more thing that went wrong with this answer, and the shape already carries a list of them.
- **One error JSON shape.** A validation failure without a caller's error is the `error` object too, `{"code": "toon_validation_failed", "message": …, "causes": [], "retryable": false}`, the keys a `DomainError` writes. Before, it was `isError: true` with no `error`, a second shape beside the `error` object the docs called the only one. The code is a string, as in every `error` object; no `ErrorCode` variant is added, so `DomainError`'s schema and its code enum are unchanged. `retryable` is false: the same input fails the same way. `as_error()` without `error()` still writes no `error` object; it marks the call failed without saying how.
- **One rule for a section's total.** The text wrote `totalCount` only above the rows (and `0` for an empty list), while the JSON wrote the declared total: `total_count(Some(1))` on two rows gave JSON `totalCount: 1` beside `returnedCount: 2` and no total in the text, and an empty list had `totalCount: 0` in the text and none in JSON. `Section::reported_total` (crate-internal) is now the one rule, read by the text's `totalCount`, the JSON section and the budget roll-up's `total` column: the total when it exceeds the rows, `0` for an empty `Toon` list, otherwise none. `total()` still returns the value as given. Output moves: the JSON `totalCount` disappears for a total at or below the rows and appears as `0` for an empty list; the roll-up shows `null` where it showed a total equal to or below the rows (spec 07's `brief.refs,5,5,false` is now `brief.refs,5,null,false`) and `0` for an empty list.
- **Hint sources compose.** `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` replaced every hint, so it dropped a `status()` report's hints and a `truncated_section()`'s `showing 2 of 4` line. It now replaces only the hints added with `hint()` and `hints()`; a part's hints keep their place. The builder convention (`xs(vec)` replaces a list) holds: the list is the caller's own.
- **`JsonObject::new` is `JsonObject::try_new`.** It returns `StructuredContentError`, and spec 03's convention is that `new` never fails and a checking constructor is `try_new`. `FromStr` is unchanged.
- **Scaling.** `tests/scaling.rs` gained cases for an error's causes, partial success, status, pipeline and a response mixing all of them, each built and rendered inside the timed region; a quadratic mutant of each (cause writers, `PartialSuccess::rows`, status rows, `Pipeline::rows`, the hint merge) fails its case.
- **Several failures are one error.** Two failed sections used to be a collision on `error` (each would write the error lines), which hid both failures behind "duplicate root key 'error'". A failed section writes no key of its own, so it cannot collide. Every failed section, and the first root-key collision, is a failure: the caller's error, or without one the first failure, is the one `error` object and the rest are its causes, in block order, on every surface. A collision still drops the sections, so the body is the error block alone.
- **Not changed:** every other rendered output is byte-identical, which the snapshot tests show.

## API

Every string these functions return for an agent is a TOON 4.4 document with no trailing newline — lists, key-value blocks, errors, status, recovery hints and help blocks alike.

### Free functions

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `renderToon` | `(opts: ToonOptions) => string` — one TOON list (`typeName`, `fields`, `rows`): the entry and a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block for any cut cell. `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse` |
| `renderHints` | `(hints: string[]) => string` — the inline array `help[N]: h1,h2` |
| `appendHints` | `(body: string, hints: string[]) => string` — append `help[N]: …` to a document, on its own line |
| `renderRecovery` | `(hints: RecoveryHint[]) => string` — the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` (`params` is `"{}"` here; an absent reason is `null`) |
| `renderKv` | `(items: KvItem[]) => string` — `key: value` lines; throws `kv_validation_failed: …` for a repeated key or a reserved key (a root key michi writes, such as `help` or `message`) |
| `renderDomainError` | `(code, message, hints, githubAnnotation?, causes?) => string` — `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, `help`. For the JSON or an MCP result, use `AgentResponse.error()`, which renders the same text |
| `renderStatus` | `(toolName, description, items, hints?) => string` — `tool`, `description`, the table `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:`, `help` |
| `renderAlreadyDone` | `(operation, summary, hints) => string` — `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary`, `help` |
| `alreadyDone` | `(stored?: string \| null) => { done: boolean, result?: string }` — classify an idempotency lookup: any stored string (even empty) is done |
| `renderPartialSuccess` | `(completed: CompletedOp[], failed: FailedOp[], skipped: SkippedOp[]) => string` (throws when an `index` repeats) — one `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:` table, a row per op sorted by `index` (the op's position in your batch; `status` is `completed`, `failed` or `skipped`; `reason` is the failure reason, the skip token or `null`), then the failed ops' `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` table |
| `renderPipeline` | `(steps: PipelineStep[]) => string` — the table `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`; `status` is a `StepStatus` label (`completed`, `outcome_unknown`, …) and `reason` is required exactly for `outcome_unknown`, `skipped` and `not_run` |
| `truncate` | `(content: string, maxChars: number) => { content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` — text that fits comes back unchanged; a longer text keeps its first `maxChars - 1` chars and ends in `…`, and the cut is reported in `removed` and `wasTruncated`, never inside `content`. Add your own hint, for example `cut ${removed} of ${originalChars} chars; pass full=true`, to the response's `help[]`. |
| `parseRetryAfter` | `(headerValue: string) => number \| null` — an RFC 9110 `Retry-After` value (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) in seconds; a past date is `0`, a malformed value `null` |
| `nextRetryDelay` | `(maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterFactor, jitterSeed, attempt, retryAfterMs?) => number \| null` — the next back-off delay in ms, or `null` once retries are used up; pass a random `jitterSeed` in `[0, 1]` per call |
| `isRetryableStatus` | `(status: number) => boolean` — `true` for 429, 502, 503 and 504; retry 502 and 504 only for idempotent requests |

### `AgentResponse` class

The primary integration point — a builder that composes TOON/KV rendering, hints, and recovery into one response. Errors, batch outcomes, pipeline state, status and already-done reports are parts of it too, so a batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is one document, one JSON object and one MCP result.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full. Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.error` | `(code, message, causes?, retryable?) => void` — report a classified error: it renders first (`error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`), `isError` is true everywhere, and the JSON carries `error: {code, message, causes, retryable}` beside `hints` and `recovery`. One per response |
| `.partialSuccess` | `(name, completed, failed, skipped) => void` — append a batch's outcomes as the list `name[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`; failed ops' recovery hints join the one `recovery` table |
| `.pipeline` | `(name, steps: PipelineStep[]) => void` — append `name[N]{id,name,status,reason}:` |
| `.status` | `(toolName, description, items: StatusItem[]) => void` — append `tool`, `description` and `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:` |
| `.alreadyDone` | `(operation, summary) => void` — append `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"error":{...},"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` (`error` and `sections` only when set) |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

Errors, batch outcomes, pipeline state, status and already-done reports are parts of it too, so a batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is one document, one JSON object and one MCP result.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full. Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.error` | `(code, message, causes?, retryable?) => void` — report a classified error: it renders first (`error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`), `isError` is true everywhere, and the JSON carries `error: {code, message, causes, retryable}` beside `hints` and `recovery`. One per response |
| `.partialSuccess` | `(name, completed, failed, skipped) => void` — append a batch's outcomes as the list `name[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`; failed ops' recovery hints join the one `recovery` table |
| `.pipeline` | `(name, steps: PipelineStep[]) => void` — append `name[N]{id,name,status,reason}:` |
| `.status` | `(toolName, description, items: StatusItem[]) => void` — append `tool`, `description` and `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:` |
| `.alreadyDone` | `(operation, summary) => void` — append `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"error":{...},"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` (`error` and `sections` only when set) |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

A quoted value runs to its closing quote (`\` escapes honored, a newline ends an unclosed one) and keeps its quotes. After a scheme word (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Negotiate`, `NTLM`, `Bot`, `Digest`) the credential is redacted and the word kept: `Authorization: Basic [REDACTED]`. `Digest` and cookie keys (`Cookie:`, `Set-Cookie:`) take the rest of the line. Any other value runs to whitespace, `&`, a quote, a backtick, `)`, `<` or `>`. `key://` is a URL, not a pair. It repeats until the text stops changing, so redacting twice equals redacting once. A fuzz target (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/redact.rs`) checks that and that a planted secret does not survive in any covered shape.

## Stability before 1.0

Until 1.0, any public item or rendered string can change in a minor release, and the changeset says how to migrate. The "format changes are major" rule above applies from 1.0. This section says where change is most likely and what we intend to hold still, so nobody builds on sand by accident. See [ADR 9](../adr/0009-v1-positioning-and-criteria.md).

**Intended design that may still change.** These are part of what michi is for, but nothing has used them yet, so their shape is not settled:

| Item | Why it may change |
| --- | --- |
| `status` (`StatusResponse`, `StatusItem`, `Health`) | No consumer has used it |
| `PartialSuccess`, `FailedOp`, `CompletedOp`, `SkippedOp` | Widened with the op index per [Spec 07](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) §4; still no consumer |
| `AlreadyDone`, `already_done()` (Node `alreadyDone`) | The check half of the idempotency design; no caller yet |
| `Sensitive<T>` | A redaction wrapper no renderer takes yet |
| `Dag::ready_by_edge` and edge kinds | New in 0.7; the argument order has changed once already |
| The `schemars` feature | JSON Schemas for MCP `outputSchema`; no consumer yet |
| `michi-pipeline`: `ExecutionError` variants, `StepObserver`, `DurableObserver`, `ExecOptions` defaults | Nothing runs pipelines yet |
| `michi-pipeline` `serde` shape of `RunRecord` | Callers persist it, so any change is called out in the changeset and old records are reported, never misread |
| `RecoveryHint.params` as a list of pairs | A representation choice that may become typed (`structured_content` became `Option<JsonObject>`) |
| The rendered `exit_code: 1` line in error blocks | Constant today; kept as the CLI-facing seam |

- Hints: empty, single, multiple, long strings
- Empty state: with and without hints

- Error: every `ErrorCode` variant — render, exit code, `Display`
- Idempotency: `already_done` format, `PartialSuccess` with mixed results
- Resilience: `parse_retry_after` (integer seconds, HTTP-date, malformed); `next_retry_delay` (backoff progression, jitter bounds, `Retry-After` respect); `is_retryable_status` (covered and uncovered codes)
- Status: every health state, degraded rendering, error rendering
- `AgentResponse` builder: every method combination, correct format dispatch

lines: - **The error block leads**, as `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code`, the reserved error keys, so no caller name can take them. One per response (a second `error()` replaces the first). A validation failure never hides it: the failure joins its causes (superseded wording, see "Response consistency" below; this said a response with both rendered the `toon_validation_failed` error for the key `error`, which hid the caller's error from the text while the JSON still carried it). `is_error()`, the JSON `isError` and MCP `isError` are true.

- **Partial success is one table**, `name[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, a row per op sorted by index (unique since `try_new`), `status` `completed`/`failed`/`skipped`, `reason` the failure reason, skip token or `null`. The quoted summary line is gone: the `status` column says the same, and as a fixed root key it collided when two batches composed. Rejected: the three tables (`completed`, `failed`, `skipped` are fixed root names a caller's sections or a second batch collide with) and a nested object per batch (a new section kind and JSON kind, and nested tables are outside the subset the strict decoder checks). A partial batch does not set `isError`: the call answered; the caller adds `error()` or `as_error()` when it failed as a whole.

- **Status** is a `Kv` section `status` (`tool`, `description`) and the `items` table, with each `KvValue` turned into the cell that renders the same token (a float rounded to its decimals, a duration as `1.5s`). **Pipeline** is a `Toon` section; `michi-pipeline` composes a run with `pipeline(name, record.to_pipeline())` and `error(record.error()?.into())`, and needs no API change. **Already done** is a `Kv` section `already_done`.

-- **NAPI** gets the same parts on the `AgentResponse` class: `error(code, message, causes?, retryable?)`, `partialSuccess(name, …)`, `pipeline(name, steps)`, `status(toolName, description, items)` and `alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, each with the standalone function's input limits and charged to the response's 16 MiB total (an error replaces its slot). `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` then cover errors, which no export did before. The standalone `render*` functions stay as text conveniences over the same writer.

+- **NAPI** gets the same parts on the `AgentResponse` class: `error(code, message, causes?, retryable?)`, `partialSuccess(name, …)`, `pipeline(name, steps)`, `status(toolName, description, items)` and `alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, each with the standalone function's input limits and charged to the response's 16 MiB total (an error replaces its slot). `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` then cover errors, which no export did before. The standalone `render*` functions stay as text conveniences over the same writer. (Superseded in 0.12: they are removed, see "One render path per outcome" below.)

- **Rendered output that moves:** `DomainError` JSON (and serde and schema) is the envelope above; `PartialSuccess` text is the one table, and an empty report is `partial_success: []` and `totalCount: 0`; an empty `Pipeline` (so `RunRecord::render` of a run with no steps) is `step: []` and `totalCount: 0`; a `StatusResponse` with no items is `items: []` and `totalCount: 0`. `DomainError` text, status and pipeline tables with rows, and the already-done text are byte-identical. `AgentResponse::render_hints_only` now includes an error's hints, as the `help` block does.

- **Proof:** `tests/compose_outcomes.rs` renders the spec 07 batch as one document checked by the strict decoder and as one JSON object, has a probe per type that could not compose before, and a property test mixes every outcome type with hostile text and checks one valid document, one JSON object and one `help`, `recovery` and `error` key. `michi-pipeline/tests/compose.rs` composes a failed run with its error.

- **Not changed:** a validation failure (`toon_validation_failed`) still has `isError` and its `error:` lines but no JSON `error` object; its code is not an `ErrorCode`, and giving it one would widen the schema's code enum for a michi-internal failure. 91-## Releasing
92-
93-[Callisto](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto) versions and publishes `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline`, `michi-graph` and `@orin-dx/michi`. They're a fixed group (`michi`), so a change to any of them releases all four on one version.
94-
95:1. With your change, add a changeset: a Markdown file in `.changeset/` (any name, e.g. `.changeset/toon-quote-tabs.md`). The front matter maps each changed package to a bump (`major`, `minor`, `patch` or `none`); the body is the changelog entry, written for users of the package.
96-
97-   ```markdown
98-   ---
99-   michi-core: patch
100-   ---
101-
102-   `render_toon` quotes cells that contain a tab.
103-   ```
104-
105-   Package names are `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline`, `michi-graph` and `michi-node` (the npm package). Changes with no user-facing effect don't need one.
106-
107-2. Merging to `main` opens or updates Callisto's version PR (`callisto/version-packages`), which bumps versions and writes the changelogs.
108-3. Merging the version PR runs the Release workflow (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`): it builds the native binaries, publishes to crates.io and npm, and creates one GitHub release tagged `michi@{version}`.
109-
110-**Post-release check.** When the run published a package to a registry, or a re-run adopted one from a failed earlier attempt, the `smoke-published` job installs that version from the public registries into clean projects on Linux x64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64 and uses it: `npm install @orin-dx/michi`, render TOON, then build a program against `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph` from crates.io. It retries for up to 10 minutes while the registries catch up. It also fails if any of the seven npm packages lacks a provenance attestation (`SMOKE_REQUIRE_ATTESTATIONS=1`): `@orin-dx/michi` is published by pnpm and the platform packages by npm, and pnpm only reads `PNPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, so releases through 0.7.1 shipped the main package unattested. A red job means the published packages are broken, so fix forward with a new release. Run the same check by hand with `just smoke-published <version>`.
111-
112-The first publish of a brand-new npm package can fail with Callisto error E157: npm accepted the upload but doesn't show the version yet. That's registry propagation lag. Wait a few minutes, then use "Re-run failed jobs" on the Release run. It adopts what already landed and publishes the rest. Don't regenerate the release intent.
113-
114-Each FSL-licensed published package carries a copy of the root `LICENSE` (`crates/michi-core/LICENSE`, `crates/michi-pipeline/LICENSE`, `packages/michi-node/LICENSE`, `packages/michi-node/npm/*/LICENSE`); `michi-graph` has its own MIT `LICENSE`. If the root license changes, copy it to each; `crates/michi-core/tests/license_copies.rs` fails until they match.
115-
116-## Commit Style
117-
118-Use imperative conventional commit prefixes: `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `ci:`.

- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

Each replacement renders the same text, and also gives you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`.

New: `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)` returns a GitHub Actions annotation, `::error title={code}::{message}`, on one line.

refactor(core)!: one render path per outcome

AgentResponse already composes every outcome, so the standalone renderers
and the second status hint channel were a second way to build the same
document: legacy surface we would otherwise promise at 1.0, and a place for
the two writers to drift.

- Node: remove renderPartialSuccess, renderPipeline, renderStatus,
  renderAlreadyDone, renderDomainError, and alreadyDone with its AlreadyDone
  type. Use the matching AgentResponse method plus renderText().
- Node: add renderGithubAnnotation(code, message), the one capability
  renderDomainError had that AgentResponse does not. It validates the code
  and takes the same 4 KiB / 1 MiB limits.
- Rust: remove resilience::render_already_done, resilience::already_done and
  the AlreadyDone enum (and their root re-exports), and StatusResponse's
  hints field and hints() builder. Status hints come from AgentResponse::hint.
- Keep each type's own render(); only the duplicates go.

Tests that covered the removed functions now go through AgentResponse;
only the alreadyDone classifier and removed hint-channel tests are deleted.

BREAKING CHANGE: the listed Node exports and Rust items are removed; see
.changeset/js-one-render-path.md and .changeset/core-one-render-path.md.

---
michi-node: minor

**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to render an error, a batch's outcomes, pipeline state, a status report or an already-done report. The standalone functions that duplicated it are removed. Below, `r` is `new AgentResponse(name)`.

- `renderDomainError(code, message, hints, false, causes)` → `r.error(code, message, causes)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderDomainError(code, message, [], true)` → `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)`.
- `renderPartialSuccess(completed, failed, skipped)` → `r.partialSuccess('partial_success', completed, failed, skipped)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderPipeline(steps)` → `r.pipeline('step', steps)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

The replacements also give you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`. Like any response, they cut a table cell over 200 characters and list it in the `truncated` block; the removed functions never cut.

New: `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)` returns a GitHub Actions annotation, `::error title={code}::{message}`, on one line.

## Result

I committed and pushed **`refactor/one-render-path`** at **`a4917e3b9553d351a3e15599955a44309fae74de`** (one commit, `refactor(core)!: one render path per outcome`), branched from `origin/fix/pipeline-start-record` (fdb9cc70). No PR, no force push, nothing pushed to main, and no session trailer.

**Stat:** 33 files, +374 / −705. That covers napi/{outcome,toon,input}.rs, napi.rs, resilience.rs, status.rs, response.rs, lib.rs, idempotency.rs, 8 Rust test files, 2 ui-fail cases, 6 docs/spec files, README.md for michi-node, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENTS.md, the 2 Node test files and the 2 new changesets.

## Removed, and what replaces each
- **Node:**
  - `renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline`, `renderStatus`, `renderAlreadyDone` → the matching `AgentResponse` method, then `.renderText()`.
  - `renderDomainError` → `AgentResponse.error`, plus `.hint` for each hint.
  - `alreadyDone` and the `AlreadyDone` JS type → nothing (the caller checks `stored != null`).
  - **New:** `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)`. It has the same code union and parse error as before, 4 KiB code / 1 MiB message, a Budget, and `catch_unwind`.
- **Rust:**
  - `resilience::render_already_done` → `AgentResponse::already_done` + `hint`/`hints`.
  - `already_done()` and the `AlreadyDone` enum, plus their root re-exports. michi-pipeline didn't use them.
  - `StatusResponse.hints` and `hints()` → `AgentResponse::hint`.
- **NAPI cleanup:** the unused `domain_error`, `partial_success`, `pipeline_table`, `status_document` and `done_or_not` helpers are gone. `STANDALONE_OUTPUT_MAX` no longer counts the 3×`MAX_STEPS` term. Docs that named the removed exports now point at `AgentResponse`.

## Changesets

`.changeset/js-one-render-path.md`:
```
---
michi-node: minor
---

**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to render an error, a batch's outcomes, pipeline state, a status report or an already-done report. The standalone functions that duplicated it are removed. Below, `r` is `new AgentResponse(name)`.

- `renderDomainError(code, message, [], true)` → `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)`.
- `renderPartialSuccess(completed, failed, skipped)` → `r.partialSuccess('partial_success', completed, failed, skipped)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderPipeline(steps)` → `r.pipeline('step', steps)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

The replacements also give you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`. Like any response, they cut a table cell over 200 characters and list it in the `truncated` block; the removed functions never cut.

New: `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)` returns a GitHub Actions annotation, `::error title={code}::{message}`, on one line.
```

`.changeset/core-one-render-path.md`:
```
---
michi-core: minor
---

**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to build an already-done report and the one place to add hints to a status report. The duplicate function and hint channel are removed.

- `render_already_done(op, summary, &hints)` → `AgentResponse::new("already_done").already_done(op, summary).hints(hints).render(OutputFormat::Text)`.
- `already_done(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` enum are removed, at `michi_core::resilience` and at the crate root: match on your stored `Option` yourself.
- `StatusResponse::hints(vec)` and its `hints` field are removed: `StatusResponse::new(..).hints(h).render()` → `AgentResponse::new("status").status(s).hints(h).render(OutputFormat::Text)`. `StatusResponse::render()` stays, without a `help` line.

A response cuts table cells over 200 characters by default; add `.truncate_cells_at(usize::MAX)` for the old uncut text.
```

## Tests
- **Rust (nextest):** 1222 → 1216.
  - Removed 6: `already_done_yes_when_stored`, `already_done_no_when_none`, `render_already_done_multiple_hints`, `render_already_done_basic` (napi), `already_done_maps_every_variant_explicitly`, and status `ac021_…hints_is_a_consuming_builder`.
  - Rewritten to go through `AgentResponse`: the already-done format and quoting tests, the status hints test, `response_consistency::hints_replaces_only_the_callers_own_hints` (now uses the error's hints), toon_blocks, compose_outcomes, line_injection, scaling, and the napi PS/pipeline/annotation tests.
  - I deleted the `resilience_exhaustive_match` ui-fail case. The `status_response_struct_literal` stderr was regenerated and I reviewed it: same E0639 error, one field fewer.
- **Node:** 186 → 183.
  - Removed: the 2 `alreadyDone` classifier tests, plus 3 count-cap cases for hint channels that no longer exist (renderStatus, renderAlreadyDone and renderDomainError hints).
  - Rewritten through `AgentResponse`: the `renderPartialSuccess` and `renderPipeline` suites (duplicate-index throw, caps, every status), the error card, causes and budget tests, status, the other count caps, and the MCP conformance cases.
  - Added 2 `renderGithubAnnotation` tests: encoding, plus code/type/size rejections.
- **Mutant:** I changed `renderGithubAnnotation` to return the plain text render. The Node test `renderGithubAnnotation writes one encoded workflow-command line` failed (182/183). I then reverted, rebuilt, and got 183/183.

## Checks (exit codes)
- `just check`: **0**
- `just test`: **0** (1216 Rust + 183 Node, no flakes).
  - Both had to run outside the sandbox, because moon locks `.git/config`.
  - In an earlier direct nextest run, 2 scaling cases needed a retry (load average was about 15–20). They passed in `just test`.
- `pnpm check` (typecheck + lint) for michi-node: **0**, with only existing lint warnings.
- **rg for removed names:** nothing left in code, tests, fuzz, scripts or examples. What remains is expected:
  - The kept `AgentResponse.alreadyDone` method, plus the internal `already_done_section` helper whose name contains `already_done`.
  - The new 06-decisions entry and the two changesets, which have to name what was removed.
  - Older 06-decisions entries. I kept these as history (PRINCIPLES says history is append-only) and added "Superseded in 0.12" notes to two of them.
  - `docs/projects/01-mvp.md`, which is marked as a historical record.
  - The 0.11 changesets, which I didn't edit.

## What I kept, and why
- **The types' own `render()`.** `StatusResponse::render`, `PartialSuccess::render`, `Pipeline::render` and `DomainError::render` each render their own document, and `RunRecord::render` relies on `Pipeline::render`.
- **NAPI input types:** `StatusItem`, `FailedOp`, `CompletedOp`, `SkippedOp` and `PipelineStep`. The `AgentResponse` methods still take them.

**Docs:** I added "Resolved 2026-11-20 — One render path per outcome" to the end of 06-decisions.

## Process note
During a WIP commit, a chained command reset my working tree. The pre-commit hook had failed because of the sandbox, and `git checkout HEAD -- .` then ran anyway. I recovered every file from the loose blobs that `git add` had written, checked the result with a diff stat, and it compiled clean.
